market_holds: Spot about $0.80 (sealed 0.8011 at 18:09 UTC on 2026-11-20), market cap about $42m, -76% from the 52-week high, +8% over 20 sessions, -1% over 5, 20-day realised vol 74.5%, about 86k shares a day. No option market. The sealed baseline has no reaction history, so I rebuilt it from Yahoo bars: print-day close-to-close moves were +25.7%, +14.8%, +11.1%, -13.9%, -30.2% (Feb 2026: founder left the board and a soft FY guide), +2.7% and +23.7% (Aug 2026: smaller loss and a revenue beat). Median absolute move is about 14%, with 5 of 7 up. Consensus for Q3: revenue $7.7-7.9m, EPS -$0.05 (Benzinga, Chartmill; undated aggregator figures). Company guide from Aug 17: Q3 revenue $7.7-7.8m, adj. EBITDA -$1.3m to -$1.2m; FY revenue $30.4-31.0m, adj. EBITDA -$6.9m to -$6.4m; adj. EBITDA breakeven on exit from 2026 and cash generation by mid-2027. The Oct 15 KPI pre-release is public and drew no move that day (0.781 to 0.781): GBV $437m against a $390-397m guide, transactions 494k against 481-490k. The stock then fell to 0.60 by Nov 5 with no company news, recovered to about 0.80 after the Nov 10 AI forwarder-platform PR, and has held there through the Nov 13 Nasdaq minimum-bid notice (compliance deadline May 10, 2027). The founder (about 6%) is fighting the board at a December AGM.
view: The print turns on Solutions, the Q4 guide and the breakeven commitment, not the platform KPIs that are already public. My arithmetic says the KPI beat buys less revenue than it looks. Platform revenue follows GBV loosely: Q1 2026 platform revenue grew 3% while GBV grew strongly, and Q2's +19% leaned on one-off Clearit tariff-refund work that management said would not repeat at that level. Q3's GBV beat came largely from elevated freight rates and fuel, and transactions beat the top of the guide by under 1%. So Q3 revenue most likely lands around the guide, roughly $7.7-7.9m, with Solutions near $4.7-4.8m against a tough $5.1m comparison. The FY guide implies Q4 revenue of $7.75-8.35m (+5% to +13% YoY) and Q4 adj. EBITDA of about -$0.7m to -$0.2m. Air rates that are still +23-28% YoY into November (Baltic/TAC) help the platform side of Q4. The Solutions ramp management promised for H2 ('conversion to improve', pipeline +30% q/q, but 'pricing pressure on renewals') is the part I cannot see, and it decides whether the FY revenue range holds or is trimmed. EBITDA has come in on guide (Q2 -$2.03m against -$2.1m to -$2.0m), and March's cost actions reach their full effect in Q4, so a reaffirmed breakeven is likely. At about $42m market cap with about $20m of cash, that matters, and it is what drove August's +24%. Against it: the market ignored the October KPI beat, a reverse split is likely to be announced at some point, and Solutions churn could force a guide cut. Net, a slight lean up on a noisy, high-variance name, well short of a recommendation.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is Solutions revenue and whether the FY guide and the Q4 breakeven hold, and no public trace shows which way Solutions went in Q3. The platform beat is already public and translates only weakly into revenue. The cost path makes a breakeven reaffirmation likely, but so far that has only been worth an in-line EBITDA. Nothing I found puts the direction at 65 or above.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 Solutions revenue up quarter on quarter with new bookings named, plus a reaffirmed FY revenue range and a Q4 EBITDA near zero, would make me lean clearly up. A Solutions decline beyond -5% YoY with a trimmed FY revenue range, or a reverse split announced with the release, would make me lean down.

self_critique: The strongest case for up is the August pattern: a beaten-down microcap with about $20m of cash at $42m market cap, a near-breakeven Q4 path and a float that moved +24% on a narrower loss; with the founder pushing, management may add buybacks or bolder targets. The strongest case for down is that Solutions has fallen two quarters running against a $5.1m Q3 comparison, and the H2 ramp in the FY guide relies on conversion management could not show in Q2. A trimmed FY range plus a reverse split statement could repeat February's -30%. Both tails are fat, which is why I hold near 50.
approach_notes: P6's 'find the line' helped: the KPIs are pre-released, so the line is Solutions plus the guide, and my own arithmetic showed the GBV beat converts only weakly into revenue. P4 pushed me to treat the ignored KPI beat as possibly unpriced, but the arithmetic answered that better than the price did. A thin baseline with no reaction history forced a rebuild from bars; that was worth it.
